t: The amendments made by the first section of this Act shall take effect as of the thirtieth day after the date of enactment of such section; except that, in any case in which a State is not authorized to issue any permit referred to in the amendments made by such first section, such amendments shall take effect in any such State as of the thirtieth day after the expiration of the next regular session of the legislature of such State which begins on or after the date of enactment of his Act.

fable.w: This is purely an effective-date provision that delays the amendments in States not yet authorized to issue the relevant permits. The tempting reading is that the references to States and state legislatures signal coordination with outside governments, but the federal government is not consulting or coordinating with any State before making a decision. The timing is simply keyed to the state legislative calendar, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: such amendments shall take effect in any such State as of the thirtieth day after the expiration of the next regular session of the legislature of such State

qwen_block.w: This section defines the effective dates of statutory amendments based on the enactment date or the expiration of state legislative sessions. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. The reference to state legislatures is purely temporal, not procedural participation.
qwen_block.s: The amendments made by the first section of this Act shall take effect as of the thirtieth day after the date of enactment of such section; except that, in any case in which a State is not authorized to issue any permit referred to in the amendments made by such first section, such amendments shall take effect in any such State as of the thirtieth day after the expiration of the next regular session of the legislature of such State which begins on or after the date of enactment of his Act.

opus.w: This is an effective-date provision. It ties when the amendments take effect to the end of a State's next legislative session. It does not require or allow any consultation, hearing, comment, advisory body or right to sue. Mentioning States and their legislatures is not enough, because the States take no part in any federal decision here.
opus.s: such amendments shall take effect in any such State as of the thirtieth day after the expiration of the next regular session of the legislature of such State

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the effective date of amendments based on the passage of time and the schedule of state legislative sessions. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or obtain input from state governments, the public, or any other outside entity before making a decision. The mention of the state legislature is purely chronological, not procedural participation.
qwen_chat.s: The amendments made by the first section of this Act shall take effect as of the thirtieth day after the date of enactment of such section; except that, in any case in which a State is not authorized to issue any permit referred to in the amendments made by such first section, such amendments shall take effect in any such State as of the thirtieth day after the expiration of the next regular session of the legislature of such State which begins on or after the date of enactment of his Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to the "legislature of such State" implies a role for state governments in the timing of the federal law's effect, which could be construed as coordination. However, the text merely sets a deadline based on the calendar of state legislative sessions; it does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from state legislators or any other outside party before making a decision. The state legislature's session is just a temporal marker, not a participatory process.
